learning_outcomes.text: Can model physical system components and model physical systems via linear graphs.
Can obtain state models of dynamics systems from system graph.
Can obtain transfer functions and time and frequency responses of systems.

syllabus_topics: System concept. Introduction to system dynamics, definitions. Modeling of physical systems. Global parameter models. Variable types.
Power and energy. Energy ports. One-port elements. Type-A, type-T, type-D and source elements.
Lineer graph representation of system elements. Oriented linear graphs of systems with one-port elements. Derivation of basic equations from system graph.
Obtaining dynamic equations of some example systems with one-port elements.
Incompatibilities in modeling and dependent elements. Impure elements.
Two-port elements. Oriented linear graphs and dynamic equations of systems with one-port and two-port elements.
Obtaining dynamic equations of some example systems with one-port and two-port elements.
State variables and state equations. Determination of state variables of systems with one-port elements from their linear graphics and derivation of state equations.
Determination of state variables of systems with one-port and two-port elements and derivation of state equations.
Linearization of nonlineer systems. Linearization around steady and non-steady operating points.
Laplace transforms. Transfer functions. Characteristic equation. Poles and zeros. Test input types and time response.
Response of systems to impulse, step and ramp inputs. Step and ramp responses of first order systems. Step responses of second order systems.
Responses of systems to sinusoidal inputs. Frequency response, amplitude ratio, phase shifting. Graphical representations of frequency response.
